neighbours.label: identity and distinctness determiners: 'same', 'own', 'each', 'distinct', 'different' marking which group something belongs to
fire: The new comet belongs to the same family as Halley's comet.
The twins were placed in different classes at the start of the year.
Volunteers will record the number of cans in each box.
The model was replaced by another one from the same agency.
The workers each brought their own tools to the site.
These risks fall into three distinct categories, explained below.
Members of the same tribe often share a family name.
Each student must hand in a separate report by Friday.
quiet: The new comet belongs to a family much larger than Halley's comet.
The twins were placed in large classes at the start of the year.
Volunteers will record the number of cans in the box.
The model was replaced by another one from a famous agency.
The workers all brought some tools to the site.
These risks fall into three broad categories, explained below.
Members of a large tribe often share a family name.
The students must hand in a short report by Friday.

notes: Top: same x10, different x4, own x3. + pole promotes ' class', ' group'.
